manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Hang the cup on the rack.

Task description: Hang the light-colored handled cup on the left side of the table on the wooden cup rack by connecting its handle to a hanging rod. Only the right arm is available, and the grasp must leave room for the handle to pass over the rod.

Success criteria: The cup must be lifted from the table, with a rack rod through the handle opening and supporting its inner side so the rack holds the cup suspended. Merely resting the cup body against the rack is insufficient.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping a cup-wall section near the opening away from the handle, with one finger inside and one outside and pads below the rim. Set an appropriate opening for wall thickness, avoiding occupation of the handle hole.
- Before closing, use both camera views if possible to confirm that the fingers are truly on the inside and outside of the cup wall, rather than just pressing against its rim. Apply only enough grip force to lift without slipping, avoiding excessive pressure on the wall.
- Choose a rod with ample space near its free end, leaving clearance for the cup and gripper from the upright and adjacent rods. Adjust handle orientation in open space outside the stand to reduce sweeping collisions.
- When inserting the rod, align its end with the free space in the cup handle and guide it through the hole's through-axis. Confirm depth from different views instead of mistaking image overlap for insertion. If contact blocks motion, back off and adjust slightly rather than pushing the rack sideways.
- Before release, lower the cup slightly so the inner handle bears its weight, then gradually relax the grasp and observe whether it slides toward the rod tip. If regrasping is needed, retain reliable support from the rod or table rather than releasing in midair.

There is still no evidence that the rod passed through the handle or supports the cup. I am adjusting the cup handle height slightly while the gripper continues to hold it.

I observed a slight displacement at the top of the mug rack, possibly related to the wrist approaching the upper rod; it recovered after retreating. I will adjust the path closer to the robot. If I still cannot obtain a clear rod-entry position, I will put the cup back on the table and end this episode.

The cup is near the table and descending in small steps while I check base support. Then I will release, lift clear of the rim, and call finish_episode.

The tool reports that the remaining operator authorization time cannot cover the next action, and the episode has entered a safe pause. I will send no further motion or gripper-release commands. The cup remains in the gripper near the table; an on-site operator must take over and check its support and the robot state. I will now call finish_episode.
